topics.label: Introduction to the Hallmarks of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic frames the lecture, sets out the learning outcomes, recaps previous material, and introduces the hallmarks of cancer framework.

topics.label: Growth Signal Autonomy and Proliferative Signaling Cascades
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in cell surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades drive self-sufficient proliferation and insensitivity to growth-inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Differentiation Blocks in Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells arrest normal lineage maturation across hematological malignancies and solid carcinomas.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: It details the molecular mechanisms and regulatory balance between p53, pro-apoptotic Bax, and anti-apoptotic BCL2 that allow cancer cells to resist programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality, Cellular Senescence, and Stress Responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells bypass telomere shortening and p53-mediated senescence checkpoints to achieve replicative immortality while transitioning toward complex systemic hallmarks.

topics.label: Reprogramming of Cellular Metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the metabolic rewiring of cancer cells, focusing on aerobic glycolysis, onco-metabolite production, and epigenetic feedback loops.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors induce new blood vessel growth to sustain oxygenation and growth through the angiogenic switch and therapeutic targeting of this pathway.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Dynamics of Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the multi-step metastatic cascade, highlighting dissemination routes, biomarkers, microenvironmental requirements, and clonal genomic features enabling distant colonization.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Closing
topics.groupedBecause: This concluding subtopic summarizes the hallmarks of cancer framework, references further reading, and closes the lecture.
